content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Confessórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Confessórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.english: This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph

content.english: On this feast day year by year receiveth

content.english: Merited honors.

content.latin: Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,

content.latin: Donec humános animávit auræ

content.latin: Ægra quæ passim iacuére membra,

content.latin: Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti

content.latin: Restituúntur.

content.latin: Psalmus 13 [1]
content.english: Psalm 13 [1]

content.latin: 13:1 Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * non est Deus.
content.english: 13:1 The fool hath said in his heart: * there is no God.

content.latin: 13:1 Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in stúdiis suis: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
content.english: 13:1 They are corrupt, and are become abominable in their ways: * there is none that doth good, no not one.

content.latin: 13:2 Dóminus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum, * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.
content.english: 13:2 The Lord hath looked down from heaven upon the children of men, * to see if there be any that understand and seek God.

content.latin: 13:3 Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
content.english: 13:3 They are all gone aside, they are become unprofitable together: * there is none that doth good: no not one.

content.latin: 13:3 Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum: linguis suis dolóse agébant * venénum áspidum sub lábiis eórum.
content.english: 13:3 Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they acted deceitfully: * the poison of asps is under their lips.

content.latin: 13:3 Quorum os maledictióne et amaritúdine plenum est: * velóces pedes eórum ad effundéndum sánguinem.
content.english: 13:3 Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness; * their feet are swift to shed blood.

content.latin: 13:3 Contrítio et infelícitas in viis eórum, et viam pacis non cognovérunt: * non est timor Dei ante óculos eórum.
content.english: 13:3 Destruction and unhappiness in their ways; and the way of peace they have not known: * there is no fear of God before their eyes.

content.latin: 13:4 Nonne cognóscent omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam sicut escam panis?
content.english: 13:4 Shall not all they know that work iniquity, * who devour my people as they eat bread?

content.latin: 13:5 Dóminum non invocavérunt, * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.
content.english: 13:5 They have not called upon the Lord: * there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.

content.latin: 13:6 Quóniam Dóminus in generatióne iusta est, consílium ínopis confudístis: * quóniam Dóminus spes eius est.
content.english: 13:6 For the Lord is in the just generation: you have confounded the counsel of the poor man; * but the Lord is his hope.

content.latin: 13:7 Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum avérterit Dóminus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.
content.english: 13:7 Who shall give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when the Lord shall have turned away the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.

content.english: Psalm 14 [2]

content.latin: 14:1 Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?
content.english: 14:1 Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? * or who shall rest in thy holy hill?

content.latin: 14:2 Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur iustítiam:
content.english: 14:2 He that walketh without blemish, * and worketh justice:

content.latin: 14:3 Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:
content.english: 14:3 He that speaketh truth in his heart, * who hath not used deceit in his tongue:

content.latin: 14:3 Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.
content.english: 14:3 Nor hath done evil to his neighbour: * nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.

content.latin: 14:4 Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu eius malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:
content.english: 14:4 In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: * but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord:

content.latin: 14:4 Qui iurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.
content.english: 14:4 He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth not; * He that hath not put out his money to usury, nor taken bribes against the innocent:

content.latin: 14:5 Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.
content.english: 14:5 He that doth these things, * shall not be moved for ever.

content.english: Psalm 16 [3]

content.latin: 16:1 Exáudi, Dómine, iustítiam meam: * inténde deprecatiónem meam.
content.english: 16:1 Hear, O Lord, my justice: * attend to my supplication.

content.latin: 16:1 Áuribus pércipe oratiónem meam, * non in lábiis dolósis.
content.english: 16:1 Give ear unto my prayer, * which proceedeth not from deceitful lips.

content.latin: 16:2 De vultu tuo iudícium meum pródeat: * óculi tui vídeant æquitátes.
content.english: 16:2 Let my judgment come forth from thy countenance: * let thy eyes behold the things that are equitable.

content.latin: 16:3 Probásti cor meum, et visitásti nocte: * igne me examinásti, et non est invénta in me iníquitas.
content.english: 16:3 Thou hast proved my heart, and visited it by night, * thou hast tried me by fire: and iniquity hath not been found in me.

content.latin: 16:4 Ut non loquátur os meum ópera hóminum: * propter verba labiórum tuórum ego custodívi vias duras.
content.english: 16:4 That my mouth may not speak the works of men: * for the sake of the words of thy lips, I have kept hard ways.

content.latin: 16:5 Pérfice gressus meos in sémitis tuis: * ut non moveántur vestígia mea.
content.english: 16:5 Perfect thou my goings in thy paths: * that my footsteps be not moved.

content.latin: 16:6 Ego clamávi, quóniam exaudísti me, Deus: * inclína aurem tuam mihi, et exáudi verba mea.
content.english: 16:6 I have cried to thee, for thou, O God, hast heard me: * O incline thy ear unto me, and hear my words.

content.latin: 16:7 Mirífica misericórdias tuas, * qui salvos facis sperántes in te.
content.english: 16:7 Shew forth thy wonderful mercies; * thou who savest them that trust in thee.

content.latin: 16:8 A resisténtibus déxteræ tuæ custódi me, * ut pupíllam óculi.
content.english: 16:8 From them that resist thy right hand keep me, * as the apple of thy eye.

content.latin: 16:8 Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege me: * a fácie impiórum qui me afflixérunt.
content.english: 16:8 Protect me under the shadow of thy wings: * from the face of the wicked who have afflicted me.

content.latin: 16:9 Inimíci mei ánimam meam circumdedérunt, ádipem suum conclusérunt: * os eórum locútum est supérbiam.
content.english: 16:9 My enemies have surrounded my soul: They have shut up their fat: * their mouth hath spoken proudly.

content.latin: 16:11 Proiciéntes me nunc circumdedérunt me: * óculos suos statuérunt declináre in terram.
content.english: 16:11 They have cast me forth, and now they have surrounded me: * they have set their eyes bowing down to the earth.

content.latin: 16:12 Suscepérunt me sicut leo parátus ad prædam: * et sicut cátulus leónis hábitans in ábditis.
content.english: 16:12 They have taken me, as a lion prepared for the prey; * and as a young lion dwelling in secret places.

content.latin: 16:13 Exsúrge, Dómine, prǽveni eum, et supplánta eum: * éripe ánimam meam ab ímpio, frámeam tuam ab inimícis manus tuæ.
content.english: 16:13 Arise, O Lord, disappoint him and supplant him; * deliver my soul from the wicked one; thy sword from the enemies of thy hand.

content.latin: 16:14 Dómine, a paucis de terra dívide eos in vita eórum: * de abscónditis tuis adimplétus est venter eórum.
content.english: 16:14 O Lord, divide them from the few of the earth in their life: * their belly is filled from thy hidden stores.

content.latin: 16:14 Saturáti sunt fíliis: * et dimisérunt relíquias suas párvulis suis.
content.english: 16:14 They are full of children: * and they have left to their little ones the rest of their substance.

content.latin: 16:15 Ego autem in iustítia apparébo conspéctui tuo: * satiábor cum apparúerit glória tua.
content.english: 16:15 But as for me, I will appear before thy sight in justice: * I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear.

content.english: Ant. I will love thee, * O Lord, who art my strength.

content.latin: Psalmus 17(2-16b) [4]
17:2 Díligam te, Dómine, fortitúdo mea: * Dóminus firmaméntum meum, et refúgium meum, et liberátor meus.
content.english: 17:2 I will love thee, O Lord, my strength: * The Lord is my firmament, my refuge, and my deliverer.

content.latin: 17:3 Deus meus adiútor meus, * et sperábo in eum.
content.english: 17:3 My God is my helper, * and in him will I put my trust.

content.latin: 17:3 Protéctor meus, et cornu salútis meæ, * et suscéptor meus.
content.english: 17:3 My protector, and the horn of my salvation, * and my support.

content.latin: 17:4 Laudans invocábo Dóminum: * et ab inimícis meis salvus ero.
content.english: 17:4 Praising, I will call upon the Lord: * and I shall be saved from my enemies.

content.latin: 17:5 Circumdedérunt me dolóres mortis: * et torréntes iniquitátis conturbavérunt me.
content.english: 17:5 The sorrows of death surrounded me: * and the torrents of iniquity troubled me.

content.latin: 17:6 Dolóres inférni circumdedérunt me: * præoccupavérunt me láquei mortis.
content.english: 17:6 The sorrows of hell encompassed me: * and the snares of death prevented me.

content.latin: 17:7 In tribulatióne mea invocávi Dóminum, * et ad Deum meum clamávi.
content.english: 17:7 In my affliction I called upon the Lord, * and I cried to my God:

content.latin: 17:7 Et exaudívit de templo sancto suo vocem meam: * et clamor meus in conspéctu eius, introívit in aures eius.
content.english: 17:7 And he heard my voice from his holy temple: * and my cry before him came into his ears.

content.latin: 17:8 Commóta est, et contrémuit terra: * fundaménta móntium conturbáta sunt, et commóta sunt, quóniam irátus est eis.
content.english: 17:8 The earth shook and trembled: * the foundations of the mountains were troubled and were moved, because he was angry with them.

content.latin: 17:9 Ascéndit fumus in ira eius: et ignis a fácie eius exársit: * carbónes succénsi sunt ab eo.
content.english: 17:9 There went up a smoke in his wrath: and a fire flamed from his face: * coals were kindled by it.

content.latin: 17:10 Inclinávit cælos, et descéndit: * et calígo sub pédibus eius.
content.english: 17:10 He bowed the heavens, and came down, * and darkness was under his feet.

content.latin: 17:11 Et ascéndit super Chérubim, et volávit: * volávit super pennas ventórum.
content.english: 17:11 And he ascended upon the cherubim, and he flew; * he flew upon the wings of the winds.

content.latin: 17:12 Et pósuit ténebras latíbulum suum, in circúitu eius tabernáculum eius: * tenebrósa aqua in núbibus áëris.
content.english: 17:12 And he made darkness his covert, his pavilion round about him: * dark waters in the clouds of the air.

content.latin: 17:13 Præ fulgóre in conspéctu eius nubes transiérunt, * grando et carbónes ignis.
content.english: 17:13 At the brightness that was before him the clouds passed, * hail and coals of fire.

content.latin: 17:14 Et intónuit de cælo Dóminus, et Altíssimus dedit vocem suam: * grando et carbónes ignis.
content.english: 17:14 And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Highest gave his voice: * hail and coals of fire.

content.latin: 17:15 Et misit sagíttas suas, et dissipávit eos: * fúlgura multiplicávit, et conturbávit eos.
content.english: 17:15 And he sent forth his arrows, and he scattered them: * he multiplied lightnings, and troubled them.

content.latin: 17:16 Et apparuérunt fontes aquárum, * et reveláta sunt fundaménta orbis terrárum:
content.english: 17:16 Then the fountains of waters appeared, * and the foundations of the world were discovered:

content.latin: 17:16 Ab increpatióne tua, Dómine, * ab inspiratióne spíritus iræ tuæ.
content.english: 17:16 At thy rebuke, O Lord, * at the blast of the spirit of thy wrath.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Díligam te, Dómine, virtus mea.
content.english: Ant. I will love thee, O Lord, who art my strength.

content.latin: Ant. Retríbuet mihi Dóminus * secúndum iustítiam meam.
content.english: Ant. The Lord will reward me * according to my justice.

content.latin: 17:17 Misit de summo, et accépit me: * et assúmpsit me de aquis multis.
content.english: 17:17 He sent from on high, and took me: * and received me out of many waters.

content.latin: 17:18 Erípuit me de inimícis meis fortíssimis, et ab his qui odérunt me: * quóniam confortáti sunt super me.
content.english: 17:18 He delivered me from my strongest enemies, and from them that hated me: * for they were too strong for me.

content.latin: 17:19 Prævenérunt me in die afflictiónis meæ: * et factus est Dóminus protéctor meus.
content.english: 17:19 They prevented me in the day of my affliction: * and the Lord became my protector.

content.latin: 17:20 Et edúxit me in latitúdinem: * salvum me fecit, quóniam vóluit me.
content.english: 17:20 And he brought me forth into a large place: * he saved me, because he was well pleased with me.

content.latin: 17:21 Et retríbuet mihi Dóminus secúndum iustítiam meam: * et secúndum puritátem mánuum meárum retríbuet mihi:
content.english: 17:21 And the Lord will reward me according to my justice; * and will repay me according to the cleanness of my hands:

content.latin: 17:22 Quia custodívi vias Dómini, * nec ímpie gessi a Deo meo.
content.english: 17:22 Because I have kept the ways of the Lord; * and have not done wickedly against my God.

content.latin: 17:23 Quóniam ómnia iudícia eius in conspéctu meo: * et iustítias eius non répuli a me.
content.english: 17:23 For all his judgments are in my sight: * and his justices I have not put away from me.

content.latin: 17:24 Et ero immaculátus cum eo: * et observábo me ab iniquitáte mea.
content.english: 17:24 And I shall be spotless with him: * and shall keep myself from my iniquity.

content.latin: 17:25 Et retríbuet mihi Dóminus secúndum iustítiam meam: * et secúndum puritátem mánuum meárum in conspéctu oculórum eius.
content.english: 17:25 And the Lord will reward me according to my justice: * and according to the cleanness of my hands before his eyes.

content.latin: 17:26 Cum sancto sanctus eris, * et cum viro innocénte ínnocens eris:
content.english: 17:26 With the holy thou wilt be holy; * and with the innocent man thou wilt be innocent:

content.latin: 17:27 Et cum elécto eléctus eris: * et cum pervérso pervertéris.
content.english: 17:27 And with the elect thou wilt be elect: * and with the perverse thou wilt be perverted.

content.latin: 17:28 Quóniam tu pópulum húmilem salvum fácies: * et óculos superbórum humiliábis.
content.english: 17:28 For thou wilt save the humble people; * but wilt bring down the eyes of the proud.

content.latin: 17:29 Quóniam tu illúminas lucérnam meam, Dómine: * Deus meus, illúmina ténebras meas.
content.english: 17:29 For thou lightest my lamp, O Lord: * O my God, enlighten my darkness.

content.latin: 17:30 Quóniam in te erípiar a tentatióne, * et in Deo meo transgrédiar murum.
content.english: 17:30 For by thee I shall be delivered from temptation; * and through my God I shall go over a wall.

content.latin: 17:31 Deus meus, impollúta via eius: elóquia Dómini igne examináta: * protéctor est ómnium sperántium in se.
content.english: 17:31 As for my God, his way is undefiled: the words of the Lord are fire-tried: * he is the protector of all that trust in him.

content.latin: 17:32 Quóniam quis Deus præter Dóminum? * aut quis Deus præter Deum nostrum?
content.english: 17:32 For who is God but the Lord? * or who is God but our God?

content.latin: 17:33 Deus, qui præcínxit me virtúte: * et pósuit immaculátam viam meam.
content.english: 17:33 God, who hath girt me with strength; * and made my way blameless.

content.latin: 17:34 Qui perfécit pedes meos tamquam cervórum, * et super excélsa státuens me.
content.english: 17:34 Who hath made my feet like the feet of harts: * and who setteth me upon high places.

content.latin: 17:35 Qui docet manus meas ad prǽlium: * et posuísti, ut arcum ǽreum, brácchia mea.
content.english: 17:35 Who teacheth my hands to war: * and thou hast made my arms like a brazen bow.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. The Lord will reward me according to my justice.

content.english: Ant. The Lord liveth, * and blessed be my God, my salvation.

content.latin: Psalmus 17(36a-51) [6]
17:36 Et dedísti mihi protectiónem salútis tuæ: * et déxtera tua suscépit me:
content.english: 17:36 Thou hast given me the protection of thy salvation: * and thy right hand hath held me up:

content.latin: 17:36 Et disciplína tua corréxit me in finem: * et disciplína tua ipsa me docébit.
content.english: 17:36 And thy discipline hath corrected me unto the end: * and thy discipline, the same shall teach me.

content.latin: 17:37 Dilatásti gressus meos subtus me: * et non sunt infirmáta vestígia mea:
content.english: 17:37 Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; * and my feet are not weakened.

content.latin: 17:38 Pérsequar inimícos meos et comprehéndam illos: * et non convértar, donec defíciant.
content.english: 17:38 I will pursue after my enemies, and overtake them: * and I will not turn again till they are consumed.

content.latin: 17:39 Confríngam illos, nec póterunt stare: * cadent subtus pedes meos.
content.english: 17:39 I will break them, and they shall not be able to stand: * they shall fall under my feet.

content.latin: 17:40 Et præcinxísti me virtúte ad bellum: * et supplantásti insurgéntes in me subtus me.
content.english: 17:40 And thou hast girded me with strength unto battle; * and hast subdued under me them that rose up against me.

content.latin: 17:41 Et inimícos meos dedísti mihi dorsum, * et odiéntes me disperdidísti.
content.english: 17:41 And thou hast made my enemies turn their back upon me, * and hast destroyed them that hated me.

content.latin: 17:42 Clamavérunt, nec erat qui salvos fáceret ad Dóminum: * nec exaudívit eos.
content.english: 17:42 They cried, but there was none to save them, to the Lord: * but he heard them not.

content.latin: 17:43 Et commínuam eos, ut púlverem ante fáciem venti: * ut lutum plateárum delébo eos.
content.english: 17:43 And I shall beat them as small as the dust before the wind; * I shall bring them to nought, like the dirt in the streets.

content.latin: 17:44 Erípies me de contradictiónibus pópuli: * constítues me in caput géntium.
content.english: 17:44 Thou wilt deliver me from the contradictions of the people; * thou wilt make me head of the Gentiles.

content.latin: 17:45 Pópulus quem non cognóvi servívit mihi: * in audítu auris obedívit mihi.
content.english: 17:45 A people which I knew not, hath served me: * at the hearing of the ear they have obeyed me.

content.latin: 17:46 Fílii aliéni mentíti sunt mihi, * fílii aliéni inveteráti sunt, et claudicavérunt a sémitis suis.
content.english: 17:46 The children that are strangers have lied to me, * strange children have faded away, and have halted from their paths.

content.latin: 17:47 Vivit Dóminus, et benedíctus Deus meus: * et exaltétur Deus salútis meæ.
content.english: 17:47 The Lord liveth, and blessed be my God, * and let the God of my salvation be exalted.

content.latin: 17:48 Deus, qui das vindíctas mihi, et subdis pópulos sub me: * liberátor meus de inimícis meis iracúndis.
content.english: 17:48 O God, who avengest me, and subduest the people under me, * my deliverer from my enraged enemies.

content.latin: 17:49 Et ab insurgéntibus in me exaltábis me: * a viro iníquo erípies me.
content.english: 17:49 And thou wilt lift me up above them that rise up against me: * from the unjust man thou wilt deliver me.

content.latin: 17:50 Proptérea confitébor tibi in natiónibus, Dómine: * et nómini tuo psalmum dicam.
content.english: 17:50 Therefore will I give glory to thee, O Lord, among the nations, * and I will sing a psalm to thy name.

content.latin: 17:51 Magníficans salútes Regis eius, et fáciens misericórdiam Christo suo David: * et sémini eius usque in sǽculum.
content.english: 17:51 Giving great deliverance to his king, and shewing mercy to David, his anointed: * and to his seed for ever.

content.latin: 19:2 Exáudiat te Dóminus in die tribulatiónis: * ‡ prótegat te nomen Dei Iacob.
content.english: 19:2 May the Lord hear thee in the day of tribulation: * ‡ may the name of the God of Jacob protect thee.

content.latin: 19:3 Mittat tibi auxílium de sancto: * et de Sion tueátur te.
content.english: 19:3 May he send thee help from the sanctuary: * and defend thee out of Sion.

content.latin: 19:4 Memor sit omnis sacrifícii tui: * et holocáustum tuum pingue fiat.
content.english: 19:4 May he be mindful of all thy sacrifices: * and may thy whole burnt offering be made fat.

content.latin: 19:5 Tríbuat tibi secúndum cor tuum: * et omne consílium tuum confírmet.
content.english: 19:5 May he give thee according to thy own heart; * and confirm all thy counsels.

content.latin: 19:6 Lætábimur in salutári tuo: * et in nómine Dei nostri magnificábimur.
content.english: 19:6 We will rejoice in thy salvation; * and in the name of our God we shall be exalted.

content.latin: 19:7 Ímpleat Dóminus omnes petitiónes tuas: * nunc cognóvi quóniam salvum fecit Dóminus Christum suum.
content.english: 19:7 The Lord fulfil all thy petitions: * now have I known that the Lord hath saved his anointed.

content.latin: 19:7 Exáudiet illum de cælo sancto suo: * in potentátibus salus déxteræ eius.
content.english: 19:7 He will hear him from his holy heaven: * the salvation of his right hand is in powers.

content.latin: 19:8 Hi in cúrribus, et hi in equis: * nos autem in nómine Dómini, Dei nostri invocábimus.
content.english: 19:8 Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: * but we will call upon the name of the Lord, our God.

content.latin: 19:9 Ipsi obligáti sunt, et cecidérunt: * nos autem surréximus et erécti sumus.
content.english: 19:9 They are bound, and have fallen: * but we are risen, and are set upright.

content.latin: 19:10 Dómine, salvum fac regem: * et exáudi nos in die, qua invocavérimus te.
content.english: 19:10 O Lord, save the king: * and hear us in the day that we shall call upon thee.

content.english: Psalm 20 [8]

content.latin: 20:2 Dómine, in virtúte tua lætábitur rex: * ‡ et super salutáre tuum exsultábit veheménter.
content.english: 20:2 The king rejoices in thy strength, O Lord; * ‡ and in thy salvation he shall rejoice exceedingly.

content.latin: 20:3 Desidérium cordis eius tribuísti ei: * et voluntáte labiórum eius non fraudásti eum.
content.english: 20:3 Thou hast given him his heart’s desire: * and hast not withholden from him the will of his lips.

content.latin: 20:4 Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis: * posuísti in cápite eius corónam de lápide pretióso.
content.english: 20:4 For thou hast prevented him with blessings of sweetness: * thou hast set on his head a crown of precious stones.

content.latin: 20:5 Vitam pétiit a te: * et tribuísti ei longitúdinem diérum in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 20:5 He asked life of thee: * and thou hast given him length of days for ever and ever.

content.latin: 20:6 Magna est glória eius in salutári tuo: * glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.
content.english: 20:6 His glory is great in thy salvation: * glory and great beauty shalt thou lay upon him.

content.latin: 20:7 Quóniam dabis eum in benedictiónem in sǽculum sǽculi: * lætificábis eum in gáudio cum vultu tuo.
content.english: 20:7 For thou shalt give him to be a blessing for ever and ever: * thou shalt make him joyful in gladness with thy countenance.

content.latin: 20:8 Quóniam rex sperat in Dómino: * et in misericórdia Altíssimi non commovébitur.
content.english: 20:8 For the king hopeth in the Lord: * and through the mercy of the most High he shall not be moved.

content.latin: 20:9 Inveniátur manus tua ómnibus inimícis tuis: * déxtera tua invéniat omnes, qui te odérunt.
content.english: 20:9 Let thy hand be found by all thy enemies: * let thy right hand find out all them that hate thee.

content.latin: 20:10 Pones eos ut clíbanum ignis in témpore vultus tui: * Dóminus in ira sua conturbábit eos, et devorábit eos ignis.
content.english: 20:10 Thou shalt make them as an oven of fire, * in the time of thy anger: the Lord shall trouble them in his wrath, and fire shall devour them.

content.latin: 20:11 Fructum eórum de terra perdes: * et semen eórum a fíliis hóminum.
content.english: 20:11 Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth: * and their seed from among the children of men.

content.latin: 20:12 Quóniam declinavérunt in te mala: * cogitavérunt consília, quæ non potuérunt stabilíre.
content.english: 20:12 For they have intended evils against thee: * they have devised counsels which they have not been able to establish.

content.latin: 20:13 Quóniam pones eos dorsum: * in relíquiis tuis præparábis vultum eórum.
content.english: 20:13 For thou shalt make them turn their back: * in thy remnants thou shalt prepare their face.

content.latin: 20:14 Exaltáre, Dómine, in virtúte tua: * cantábimus et psallémus virtútes tuas.
content.english: 20:14 Be thou exalted, O Lord, in thy own strength: * we will sing and praise thy power.

content.english: Psalm 29 [9]

content.latin: 29:2 Exaltábo te, Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me: * ‡ nec delectásti inimícos meos super me.
content.english: 29:2 I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me: * ‡ and hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me.

content.latin: 29:3 Dómine, Deus meus, clamávi ad te, * et sanásti me.
content.english: 29:3 O Lord my God, I have cried to thee, * and thou hast healed me.

content.latin: 29:4 Dómine, eduxísti ab inférno ánimam meam: * salvásti me a descendéntibus in lacum.
content.english: 29:4 Thou hast brought forth, O Lord, my soul from hell: * thou hast saved me from them that go down into the pit.

content.latin: 29:5 Psállite Dómino, sancti eius: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis eius.
content.english: 29:5 Sing to the Lord, O ye his saints: * and give praise to the memory of his holiness.

content.latin: 29:6 Quóniam ira in indignatióne eius: * et vita in voluntáte eius.
content.english: 29:6 For wrath is in his indignation; * and life in his good will.

content.latin: 29:6 Ad vésperum demorábitur fletus: * et ad matutínum lætítia.
content.english: 29:6 In the evening weeping shall have place, * and in the morning gladness.

content.latin: 29:7 Ego autem dixi in abundántia mea: * Non movébor in ætérnum.
content.english: 29:7 And in my abundance I said: * I shall never be moved.

content.latin: 29:8 Dómine, in voluntáte tua, * præstitísti decóri meo virtútem.
content.english: 29:8 O Lord, in thy favour, * thou gavest strength to my beauty.

content.latin: 29:8 Avertísti fáciem tuam a me, * et factus sum conturbátus.
content.english: 29:8 Thou turnedst away thy face from me, * and I became troubled.

content.latin: 29:9 Ad te, Dómine, clamábo: * et ad Deum meum deprecábor.
content.english: 29:9 To thee, O Lord, will I cry: * and I will make supplication to my God.

content.latin: 29:10 Quæ utílitas in sánguine meo, * dum descéndo in corruptiónem?
content.english: 29:10 What profit is there in my blood, * whilst I go down to corruption?

content.latin: 29:10 Numquid confitébitur tibi pulvis, * aut annuntiábit veritátem tuam?
content.english: 29:10 Shall dust confess to thee, * or declare thy truth?

content.latin: 29:11 Audívit Dóminus, et misértus est mei: * Dóminus factus est adiútor meus.
content.english: 29:11 The Lord hath heard, and hath had mercy on me: * the Lord became my helper.

content.latin: 29:12 Convertísti planctum meum in gáudium mihi: * conscidísti saccum meum, et circumdedísti me lætítia:
content.english: 29:12 Thou hast turned for me my mourning into joy: * thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness:

content.latin: 29:13 Ut cantet tibi glória mea, et non compúngar: * Dómine, Deus meus, in ætérnum confitébor tibi.
content.english: 29:13 To the end that my glory may sing to thee, and I may not regret: * O Lord my God, I will give praise to thee for ever.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Ille nos benedícat, qui sine fine vivit et regnat.
content.english: Benediction. May His blessing be upon us who doth live and reign for ever.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: De libro primo Regum
content.english: Lesson from the first book of Samuel

content.latin: 25 Et dixit unus quíspiam de Israël: Num vidístis virum hunc qui ascéndit? Ad exprobrándum enim Israéli ascéndit. Virum ergo, qui percússerit eum, ditábit rex divítiis magnis et fíliam suam dabit ei et domum patris eius fáciet absque tribúto in Israël.
content.english: 25 And some one of Israel said: Have you seen this man that is come up, for he is come up to defy Israel. And the man that shall slay him, the king will enrich with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and will make his father's house free from tribute in Israel.

content.latin: 26 Et ait David ad viros, qui stabant secum, dicens: Quid dábitur viro, qui percússerit Philisthǽum hunc et túlerit oppróbrium de Israël? Quis enim est hic Philisthǽus incircumcísus, qui exprobrávit ácies Dei vivéntis?
content.english: 26 And David spoke to the men that stood by him, saying: What shall be given to the man that shall kill this Philistine, and shall take away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Recordáre, Dómine, testaménti tui, et dic Angelo percutiénti: Cesset iam manus tua,
content.english: ℟. Remember, O Lord, thy covenant, and say unto the destroying Angel: Stay now thine hand;

content.latin: * Ut non desolétur terra, et ne perdas omnem ánimam vivam.
content.english: * That the land be not utterly laid waste, and that thou destroy not every living soul.

content.latin: ℣. Ego sum qui peccávi, ego qui iníque egi: isti qui oves sunt, quid fecérunt? Avertátur, óbsecro, furor tuus, Dómine, a pópulo tuo.
content.english: ℣. Even I it is that have sinned, and done evil indeed; but these sheep, what have they done? Let thine anger, I pray thee, O Lord, be turned away from thy people.

content.latin: ℟. Ut non desolétur terra, et ne perdas omnem ánimam vivam.
content.english: ℟. That the land be not utterly laid waste, and that Thou destroy not every living soul.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Cuius festum cólimus, ipse intercédat pro nobis ad Dóminum.
content.english: Benediction. He whose feast-day we are keeping, be our Advocate with God.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 31 Audíta sunt autem verba, quæ locútus est David, et annuntiáta in conspéctu Saul.
content.english: 31 And the words which David spoke were heard, and were rehearsed before Saul.

content.latin: 32 Ad quem cum fuísset addúctus, locútus est ei: Non cóncidat cor cuiúsquam in eo: ego servus tuus vadam et pugnábo advérsus Philisthǽum.
content.english: 32 And when he was brought to him, he said to him: Let not any man's heart be dismayed in him: I thy servant will go, and will fight against the Philistine.

content.latin: 33 Et ait Saul ad David: Non vales resistere Philisthǽo isti nec pugnáre advérsus eum, quia puer es, hic autem vir bellátor est ab adulescéntia sua.
content.english: 33 And Saul said to David: Thou art not able to withstand this Philistine, nor to fight against him: for thou art but a boy, but he is a warrior from his youth.

content.latin: Paulínus, anno reparátæ salútis trecentésimo quinquagésimo tértio a claríssima cívium Romanórum família Burdígalæ natus, senatória dignitáte potítus est. Nolæ consul renuntiátus, divíno lúmine tactus consulátum dimísit, et, Burdígalam revérsus, a beáto Delphíno baptizátus est. Dein, bonórum quibus abundábat prétio paupéribus distribúto, in Hispániam secéssit, ubi présbyter ordinátur. Nolam cum rediísset, penes sancti Felícis sepúlcrum monastérium cóndidit, sociísque adscítis, cœnobíticam vitam eámque arctíssimam est aggréssus. Percrebrescénte eius sanctimóniæ fama, ad Nolánum episcopátum evéhitur, quo in múnere admiránda pietátis, patiéntiæ ac potíssimum caritátis exémpla relíquit. Multa ad sacram doctrínam pertinéntia scripsit, atque ínsuper eloquéntiæ et poéseos laude excélluit. Vastáta a Gothis Campánia, facultátes omnes in aléndos páuperes et captívos rediméndos cóntulit. Póstea vero, Vándalis eásdem regiónes infestántibus, cum nil ámplius erogándum habéret, se ipsum pro fílio cuiúsdam víduæ in servitútem trádidit, et in Africam ductus est. Tandem, Dei ope libertáte donátus, Nolæ placidíssimo éxitu obdormívit in Dómino.
content.english: Paulinus, born in the year of restored salvation 353 of a very famous Roman family of Bordeaux, acquired the dignity of senator. He was made consul of Nola, but a divine light prompted him to renounce the consulship and return to Bordeaux, where he was baptized by St. Delphinus. Then, giving to the poor the large sum obtained by the sale of his goods, he went to Spain, where he was ordained priest. When he returned to Nola, he built a monastery near the grave of St. Felix and, with the companions who joined him, undertook a most austere cenobitical life. As the fame of his holiness grew, he was elevated to the bishopric of Nola, in which office he left an example of wonderful devotion, patience, and especially charity. He wrote many works on sacred doctrine and also gained a reputation for eloquence and poetry. When Campania was devastated by the Goths, he used all his goods to feed the poor and redeem captives. And later, when the Vandals infested the same region and he had nothing more to give, he gave himself into slavery for the son of a widow, and was taken to Africa. At length, restored to liberty, by the hand of God, he died a peaceful death in the Lord at Nola.

content.english: In England, the holy Queen and Virgin Etheldreda, who passed away to be with the Lord, illustrious for holiness and miracles whose body was found incorrupt eleven years after her death, [in the year 679.]

content.latin: Item Romæ sanctæ Agrippínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quæ sub Valeriáno Imperatóre martýrium consummávit. Ipsíus autem corpus, in Sicíliam translátum ac Menis cónditum, multis miráculis corúscat.
content.english: At Rome, the holy Priest John, who was beheaded, under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, in front of the image of the sun upon the old Salarian Way. His body was buried by the blessed Priest Concordius, hard by the martyrs' burial-place.

content.latin: Sútrii, in Túscia, sancti Felícis Presbýteri, cuius os támdiu iussit Túrcius Præféctus lápide contúndi, donec ipse Felix emítteret spíritum.
content.english: Likewise at Rome, under the Emperor Valerian, the holy Virgin and martyr Agrippina, whose body was taken to Sicily and is distinguished for many miracles.

content.latin: Nicomedíæ commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui, témpore Diocletiáni, in móntibus et spelúncis laténtes, pro Christi nómine martýrium læto ánimo subiérunt.
content.english: At Sutri, in Tuscany, the holy Priest Felix, whose mouth the Prefect Turcius ordered to be pounded with a stone until he died.

content.latin: Philadelphíæ, in Arábia, sanctórum Mártyrum Zenónis, eiúsque servi Zenæ. Hic dómini sui vincti caténas exósculans, eúmque rogans ut se in torméntis partícipem dignarétur habére, a milítibus tentus est, et cum ipso dómino parem martýrii corónam accépit.
content.english: At Nicomedia are commemorated very many holy martyrs who, in the time of Diocletian, wandered in deserts and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth, and for Christ's Name's sake, underwent martyrdom with joy.

content.latin: Augústæ Taurinórum sancti Ioséphi Cafásso, Sacerdótis, qui levítis pietáte et sciéntia augéndis atque damnátis cápite Deo conciliándis fuit illústris, et a Pio Papa Duodécimo inter sanctos Cǽlites adscríptus est.
content.english: At Philadelphia, in Arabia, the holy martyr Zeno and Zenas his slave. When Zeno was bound Zenas kissed his chains, and besought him to be pleased to have him for a sharer in his torments, whereupon the soldiers took him, and he and his master received the same crown of martyrdom together, [in the year 304.]

content.latin: Psalmus 26(1-6) [1]
26:1 Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?
content.english: 26:1 The Lord is my light and my salvation, * whom shall I fear?

content.latin: 26:1 Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?
content.english: 26:1 The Lord is the protector of my life: * of whom shall I be afraid?

content.latin: 26:2 Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:
content.english: 26:2 Whilst the wicked draw near against me, * to eat my flesh.

content.latin: 26:2 Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.
content.english: 26:2 My enemies that trouble me, * have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.

content.latin: 26:3 Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.
content.english: 26:3 If armies in camp should stand together against me, * my heart shall not fear.

content.latin: 26:3 Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.
content.english: 26:3 If a battle should rise up against me, * in this will I be confident.

content.latin: 26:4 Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
content.english: 26:4 One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; * that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.

content.latin: 26:4 Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum eius.
content.english: 26:4 That I may see the delight of the Lord, * and may visit his temple.

content.latin: 26:5 Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
content.english: 26:5 For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; * in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.

content.latin: 26:6 In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.
content.english: 26:6 He hath exalted me upon a rock: * and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies.

content.latin: 26:6 Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo eius hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
content.english: 26:6 I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: * I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 26:7 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.
content.english: 26:7 Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: * have mercy on me and hear me.

content.latin: 26:8 Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
content.english: 26:8 My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: * thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.

content.latin: 26:9 Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.
content.english: 26:9 Turn not away thy face from me; * decline not in thy wrath from thy servant.

content.latin: 26:9 Adiútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
content.english: 26:9 Be thou my helper, * forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

content.latin: 26:10 Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
content.english: 26:10 For my father and my mother have left me: * but the Lord hath taken me up.

content.latin: 26:11 Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
content.english: 26:11 Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, * and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.

content.latin: 26:12 Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
content.english: 26:12 Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; * for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.

content.latin: 26:13 Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.
content.english: 26:13 I believe to see the good things of the Lord * in the land of the living.

content.latin: 26:14 Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
content.english: 26:14 Expect the Lord, do manfully, * and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.

content.latin: 27:1 Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: * nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.
content.english: 27:1 Unto thee will I cry, O Lord: my God, be not thou silent to me: * lest if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.

content.latin: 27:2 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: * dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.
content.english: 27:2 Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray to thee; * when I lift up my hands to thy holy temple.

content.latin: 27:3 Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: * et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me.
content.english: 27:3 Draw me not away together with the wicked; * and with the workers of iniquity destroy me not:

content.latin: 27:3 Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, * mala autem in córdibus eórum.
content.english: 27:3 Who speak peace with their neighbour, * but evils are in their hearts.

content.latin: 27:4 Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, * et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum.
content.english: 27:4 Give them according to their works, * and according to the wickedness of their inventions.

content.latin: 27:4 Secúndum ópera mánuum eórum tríbue illis: * redde retributiónem eórum ipsis.
content.english: 27:4 According to the works of their hands give thou to them: * render to them their reward.

content.latin: 27:5 Quóniam non intellexérunt ópera Dómini, et in ópera mánuum eius * déstrues illos, et non ædificábis eos.
content.english: 27:5 Because they have not understood the works of the Lord, and the operations of his hands: * thou shalt destroy them, and shalt not build them up.

content.latin: 27:6 Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam exaudívit vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
content.english: 27:6 Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath heard the voice of my supplication.

content.latin: 27:7 Dóminus adiútor meus, et protéctor meus: * in ipso sperávit cor meum, et adiútus sum.
content.english: 27:7 The Lord is my helper and my protector: * in him hath my heart confided, and I have been helped.

content.latin: 27:7 Et reflóruit caro mea: * et ex voluntáte mea confitébor ei.
content.english: 27:7 And my flesh hath flourished again, * and with my will I will give praise to him.

content.latin: 27:8 Dóminus fortitúdo plebis suæ: * et protéctor salvatiónum Christi sui est.
content.english: 27:8 The Lord is the strength of his people, * and the protector of the salvation of his anointed.

content.latin: 27:9 Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, et bénedic hereditáti tuæ: * et rege eos, et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: 27:9 Save, O Lord, thy people, and bless thy inheritance: * and rule them and exalt them for ever.

content.latin: Rector potens, verax Deus,
content.english: O God of truth, O Lord of might,

content.latin: Qui témperas rerum vices,
content.english: Who orderest time and change aright,

content.latin: Splendóre mane illúminas,
content.english: Who send’st the early morning ray,

content.latin: Et ígnibus merídiem:
content.english: And light’st the glow of perfect day:

content.latin: Exstíngue flammas lítium,
content.english: Extinguish thou each sinful fire,

content.latin: Aufer calórem nóxium,
content.english: And banish every ill desire;

content.latin: Confer salútem córporum,
content.english: And while thou keep’st the body whole,

content.latin: Verámque pacem córdium.
content.english: Shed forth thy peace upon the soul.

content.english: Almighty Father, hear our cry,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, our Lord most High,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

content.latin: Ant. In tua iustítia * líbera me, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. Deliver me * in thy justice, O Lord.

content.latin: Psalmus 30(2-9) [1]
30:2 In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in iustítia tua líbera me.
content.english: 30:2 In thee, O Lord, have I hoped, let me never be confounded: * deliver me in thy justice.

content.latin: 30:3 Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * accélera ut éruas me.
content.english: 30:3 Bow down thy ear to me: * make haste to deliver me.

content.latin: 30:3 Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in domum refúgii: * ut salvum me fácias.
content.english: 30:3 Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a house of refuge, * to save me.

content.latin: 30:4 Quóniam fortitúdo mea, et refúgium meum es tu: * et propter nomen tuum dedúces me, et enútries me.
content.english: 30:4 For thou art my strength and my refuge; * and for thy name’s sake thou wilt lead me, and nourish me.

content.latin: 30:5 Edúces me de láqueo hoc, quem abscondérunt mihi: * quóniam tu es protéctor meus.
content.english: 30:5 Thou wilt bring me out of this snare, which they have hidden for me: * for thou art my protector.

content.latin: 30:6 In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: * redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.
content.english: 30:6 Into thy hands I commend my spirit: * thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, the God of truth.

content.latin: 30:7 Odísti observántes vanitátes, * supervácue.
content.english: 30:7 Thou hast hated them that regard vanities, * to no purpose.

content.latin: 30:7 Ego autem in Dómino sperávi: * exsultábo, et lætábor in misericórdia tua.
content.english: 30:7 But I have hoped in the Lord: * I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy.

content.latin: 30:8 Quóniam respexísti humilitátem meam, * salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam.
content.english: 30:8 For thou hast regarded my humility, * thou hast saved my soul out of distresses.

content.latin: 30:9 Nec conclusísti me in mánibus inimíci: * statuísti in loco spatióso pedes meos.
content.english: 30:9 And thou hast not shut me up in the hands of the enemy: * thou hast set my feet in a spacious place.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 30:10 Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam tríbulor: * conturbátus est in ira óculus meus, ánima mea, et venter meus:
content.english: 30:10 Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am afflicted: * my eye is troubled with wrath, my soul, and my belly:

content.latin: 30:11 Quóniam defécit in dolóre vita mea: * et anni mei in gemítibus.
content.english: 30:11 For my life is wasted with grief: * and my years in sighs.

content.latin: 30:11 Infirmáta est in paupertáte virtus mea: * et ossa mea conturbáta sunt.
content.english: 30:11 My strength is weakened through poverty * and my bones are disturbed.

content.latin: 30:12 Super omnes inimícos meos factus sum oppróbrium et vicínis meis valde: * et timor notis meis.
content.english: 30:12 I am become a reproach among all my enemies, and very much to my neighbours; * and a fear to my acquaintance.

content.latin: 30:12 Qui vidébant me, foras fugérunt a me: * oblivióni datus sum, tamquam mórtuus a corde.
content.english: 30:12 They that saw me without fled from me. * I am forgotten as one dead from the heart.

content.latin: 30:13 Factus sum tamquam vas pérditum: * quóniam audívi vituperatiónem multórum commorántium in circúitu.
content.english: 30:13 I am become as a vessel that is destroyed. * For I have heard the blame of many that dwell round about.

content.latin: 30:14 In eo dum convenírent simul advérsum me, * accípere ánimam meam consiliáti sunt.
content.english: 30:14 While they assembled together against me, * they consulted to take away my life.

content.latin: 30:15 Ego autem in te sperávi, Dómine: * dixi: Deus meus es tu: in mánibus tuis sortes meæ.
content.english: 30:15 But I have put my trust in thee, O Lord: * I said: Thou art my God. My lots are in thy hands.

content.latin: 30:16 Éripe me de manu inimicórum meórum, * et a persequéntibus me.
content.english: 30:16 Deliver me out of the hands of my enemies; * and from them that persecute me

content.latin: 30:17 Illústra fáciem tuam super servum tuum, salvum me fac in misericórdia tua: * Dómine, non confúndar, quóniam invocávi te.
content.english: 30:17 Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; save me in thy mercy. * Let me not be confounded, O Lord, for I have called upon thee.

content.latin: 30:18 Erubéscant ímpii, et deducántur in inférnum: * muta fiant lábia dolósa.
content.english: 30:18 Let the wicked be ashamed, and be brought down to hell. * Let deceitful lips be made dumb.

content.latin: 30:19 Quæ loquúntur advérsus iustum iniquitátem: * in supérbia, et in abusióne.
content.english: 30:19 Which speak iniquity against the just, * with pride and abuse.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 30:20 Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ, Dómine, * quam abscondísti timéntibus te.
content.english: 30:20 How great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord, * which thou hast hidden for them that fear thee!

content.latin: 30:20 Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te, * in conspéctu filiórum hóminum.
content.english: 30:20 Which thou hast wrought for them that hope in thee, * in the sight of the sons of men.

content.latin: 30:21 Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ * a conturbatióne hóminum.
content.english: 30:21 Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy face, * from the disturbance of men.

content.latin: 30:21 Próteges eos in tabernáculo tuo * a contradictióne linguárum.
content.english: 30:21 Thou shalt protect them in thy tabernacle * from the contradiction of tongues.

content.latin: 30:22 Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam mirificávit misericórdiam suam mihi in civitáte muníta.
content.english: 30:22 Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath shewn his wonderful mercy to me in a fortified city.

content.latin: 30:23 Ego autem dixi in excéssu mentis meæ: * Proiéctus sum a fácie oculórum tuórum.
content.english: 30:23 But I said in the excess of my mind: * I am cast away from before thy eyes.

content.latin: 30:23 Ídeo exaudísti vocem oratiónis meæ, * dum clamárem ad te.
content.english: 30:23 Therefore thou hast heard the voice of my prayer, * when I cried to thee.

content.latin: 30:24 Dilígite Dóminum omnes sancti eius: * quóniam veritátem requíret Dóminus, et retríbuet abundánter faciéntibus supérbiam.
content.english: 30:24 O love the Lord, all ye his saints: * for the Lord will require truth, and will repay them abundantly that act proudly.

content.latin: 30:25 Viríliter ágite, et confortétur cor vestrum, * omnes, qui sperátis in Dómino.
content.english: 30:25 Do ye manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, * all ye that hope in the Lord.

content.latin: Non est invéntus símilis illi, qui conserváret legem Excélsi: ídeo iureiurándo fecit illum Dóminus créscere in plebem suam.
content.english: There was not found the like to him in glory, who kept the law of the most High, and was in covenant with him. Therefore by an oath he gave him glory in his posterity, that he should increase in his people.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.english: ℟. The Lord hath chosen him * for a Priest unto Himself.

content.latin: ℣. Ad sacrificándum ei hóstiam laudis.
content.english: ℣. To offer up unto Him the sacrifice of praise.

content.english: ℟. The Lord hath chosen him * for a Priest unto Himself.

content.latin: ℣. Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum.
content.english: ℣. Thou art a Priest for ever.

content.latin: ℟. Secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
content.english: ℟. After the order of Melchisedek.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui ómnia pro te in hoc sǽculo relinquéntibus, céntuplum in futúro et vitam ætérnam promisísti: concéde propítius; ut, sancti Pontíficis Paulíni vestígiis inhæréntes, valeámus terréna despícere et sola cæléstia desideráre:
content.english: O God, who hast promised to them that leave all things in this world for thy sake to receive an hundredfold, and everlasting life in that which is to come: mercifully grant; that, following in the footsteps of thy blessed Saint Paulinus, we may be enabled to despise all things that are earthly, and to desire only those things that are heavenly.

content.latin: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Rerum, Deus, tenax vigor,
content.english: O strength and stay upholding all creation,

content.latin: Immótus in te pérmanens,
content.english: Who ever dost thyself unmoved abide,

content.latin: Lucis diúrnæ témpora
content.english: Yet day by day the light in due gradation

content.latin: Succéssibus detérminans:
content.english: From hour to hour through all its changes guide:

content.latin: Largíre lumen véspere,
content.english: Grant to life’s day a calm unclouded ending,

content.latin: Quo vita nusquam décidat,
content.english: An eve untouched by shadows of decay,

content.latin: Sed prǽmium mortis sacræ
content.english: The brightness of a holy death-bed blending

content.latin: Perénnis instet glória.
content.english: With dawning glories of th’ eternal day.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Hear us, O Father, gracious and forgiving,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: And thou, O Christ, the co-eternal Word,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost, by all things living

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Now and to endless ages art adored.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Exsultáte, iusti, * et gloriámini, omnes recti corde.
content.english: Ant. Rejoice ye just, * and glory, all ye right of heart.

content.latin: Psalmus 31 [1]
content.english: Psalm 31 [1]

content.latin: 31:1 Beáti quorum remíssæ sunt iniquitátes: * et quorum tecta sunt peccáta.
content.english: 31:1 Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven * and whose sins are covered.

content.latin: 31:2 Beátus vir, cui non imputávit Dóminus peccátum, * nec est in spíritu eius dolus.
content.english: 31:2 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord hath not imputed sin, * and in whose spirit there is no guile.

content.latin: 31:3 Quóniam tácui, inveteravérunt ossa mea, * dum clamárem tota die.
content.english: 31:3 Because I was silent my bones grew old; * whilst I cried out all the day long.

content.latin: 31:4 Quóniam die ac nocte graváta est super me manus tua: * convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.
content.english: 31:4 For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: * I am turned in my anguish, whilst the thorn is fastened.

content.latin: 31:5 Delíctum meum cógnitum tibi feci: * et iniustítiam meam non abscóndi.
content.english: 31:5 I have acknowledged my sin to thee, * and my injustice I have not concealed.

content.latin: 31:5 Dixi: Confitébor advérsum me iniustítiam meam Dómino: * et tu remisísti impietátem peccáti mei.
content.english: 31:5 I said I will confess against myself my injustice to the Lord: * and thou hast forgiven the wickedness of my sin.

content.latin: 31:6 Pro hac orábit ad te omnis sanctus, * in témpore opportúno.
content.english: 31:6 For this shall every one that is holy pray to thee * in a seasonable time.

content.latin: 31:6 Verúmtamen in dilúvio aquárum multárum, * ad eum non approximábunt.
content.english: 31:6 And yet in a flood of many waters, * they shall not come nigh unto him.

content.latin: 31:7 Tu es refúgium meum a tribulatióne, quæ circúmdedit me: * exsultátio mea, érue me a circumdántibus me.
content.english: 31:7 Thou art my refuge from the trouble which hath encompassed me: * my joy, deliver me from them that surround me.

content.latin: 31:8 Intelléctum tibi dabo, et ínstruam te in via hac, qua gradiéris: * firmábo super te óculos meos.
content.english: 31:8 I will give thee understanding, and I will instruct thee in this way, in which thou shalt go: * I will fix my eyes upon thee.

content.latin: 31:9 Nolíte fíeri sicut equus et mulus, * quibus non est intelléctus.
content.english: 31:9 Do not become like the horse and the mule, * who have no understanding.

content.latin: 31:9 In camo et freno maxíllas eórum constrínge, * qui non appróximant ad te.
content.english: 31:9 With bit and bridle bind fast their jaws, * who come not near unto thee.

content.latin: 31:10 Multa flagélla peccatóris, * sperántem autem in Dómino misericórdia circúmdabit.
content.english: 31:10 Many are the scourges of the sinner, * but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord.

content.latin: 31:11 Lætámini in Dómino et exsultáte, iusti, * et gloriámini, omnes recti corde.
content.english: 31:11 Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye just, * and glory, all ye right of heart.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 32:1 Exsultáte, iusti, in Dómino: * rectos decet collaudátio.
content.english: 32:1 Rejoice in the Lord, O ye just: * praise becometh the upright.

content.latin: 32:2 Confitémini Dómino in cíthara: * in psaltério decem chordárum psállite illi.
content.english: 32:2 Give praise to the Lord on the harp; * sing to him with the psaltery, the instrument of ten strings.

content.latin: 32:3 Cantáte ei cánticum novum: * bene psállite ei in vociferatióne.
content.english: 32:3 Sing to him a new canticle, * sing well unto him with a loud noise.

content.latin: 32:4 Quia rectum est verbum Dómini, * et ómnia ópera eius in fide.
content.english: 32:4 For the word of the Lord is right, * and all his works are done with faithfulness.

content.latin: 32:5 Díligit misericórdiam et iudícium: * misericórdia Dómini plena est terra.
content.english: 32:5 He loveth mercy and judgment; * the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.

content.latin: 32:6 Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt: * et spíritu oris eius omnis virtus eórum.
content.english: 32:6 By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; * and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth:

content.latin: 32:7 Cóngregans sicut in utre aquas maris: * ponens in thesáuris abýssos.
content.english: 32:7 Gathering together the waters of the sea, as in a vessel; * laying up the depths in storehouses.

content.latin: 32:8 Tímeat Dóminum omnis terra: * ab eo autem commoveántur omnes inhabitántes orbem.
content.english: 32:8 Let all the earth fear the Lord, * and let all the inhabitants of the world be in awe of him.

content.latin: 32:9 Quóniam ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 32:9 For he spoke and they were made: * he commanded and they were created.

content.latin: 32:10 Dóminus díssipat consília géntium: * réprobat autem cogitatiónes populórum, et réprobat consília príncipum.
content.english: 32:10 The Lord bringeth to nought the counsels of nations; * and he rejecteth the devices of people, and casteth away the counsels of princes.

content.latin: 32:11 Consílium autem Dómini in ætérnum manet: * cogitatiónes cordis eius in generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 32:11 But the counsel of the Lord standeth for ever: * the thoughts of his heart to all generations.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 32:12 Beáta gens, cuius est Dóminus, Deus eius: * pópulus, quem elégit in hereditátem sibi.
content.english: 32:12 Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord: * the people whom he hath chosen for his inheritance.

content.latin: 32:13 De cælo respéxit Dóminus: * vidit omnes fílios hóminum.
content.english: 32:13 The Lord hath looked from heaven: * he hath beheld all the sons of men.

content.latin: 32:14 De præparáto habitáculo suo * respéxit super omnes, qui hábitant terram.
content.english: 32:14 From his habitation which he hath prepared, * he hath looked upon all that dwell on the earth.

content.latin: 32:15 Qui finxit sigillátim corda eórum: * qui intéllegit ómnia ópera eórum.
content.english: 32:15 He who hath made the hearts of every one of them: * who understandeth all their works.

content.latin: 32:16 Non salvátur rex per multam virtútem: * et gigas non salvábitur in multitúdine virtútis suæ.
content.english: 32:16 The king is not saved by a great army: * nor shall the giant be saved by his own great strength.

content.latin: 32:17 Fallax equus ad salútem: * in abundántia autem virtútis suæ non salvábitur.
content.english: 32:17 Vain is the horse for safety: * neither shall he be saved by the abundance of his strength.

content.latin: 32:18 Ecce, óculi Dómini super metuéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia eius:
content.english: 32:18 Behold the eyes of the Lord are on them that fear him: * and on them that hope in his mercy.

content.latin: 32:19 Ut éruat a morte ánimas eórum: * et alat eos in fame.
content.english: 32:19 To deliver their souls from death; * and feed them in famine.

content.latin: 32:20 Ánima nostra sústinet Dóminum: * quóniam adiútor et protéctor noster est.
content.english: 32:20 Our soul waiteth for the Lord: * for he is our helper and protector.

content.latin: 32:21 Quia in eo lætábitur cor nostrum: * et in nómine sancto eius sperávimus.
content.english: 32:21 For in him our heart shall rejoice: * and in his holy name we have trusted.

content.latin: 32:22 Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos: * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: 32:22 Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, * as we have hoped in thee.

content.latin: 114:2 Quia inclinávit aurem suam mihi: * et in diébus meis invocábo.
content.english: 114:2 Because he hath inclined his ear unto me: * and in my days I will call upon him.

content.latin: 114:3 Circumdedérunt me dolóres mortis: * et perícula inférni invenérunt me.
content.english: 114:3 The sorrows of death have compassed me: * and the perils of hell have found me.

content.latin: 114:3 Tribulatiónem et dolórem invéni: * et nomen Dómini invocávi.
content.english: 114:3 I met with trouble and sorrow: * and I called upon the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 114:4 O Dómine, líbera ánimam meam: * miséricors Dóminus, et iustus, et Deus noster miserétur.
content.english: 114:4 O Lord, deliver my soul. * The Lord is merciful and just, and our God sheweth mercy.

content.latin: 114:6 Custódiens párvulos Dóminus: * humiliátus sum, et liberávit me.
content.english: 114:6 The Lord is the keeper of little ones: * I was humbled, and he delivered me.

content.latin: 114:7 Convértere, ánima mea, in réquiem tuam: * quia Dóminus benefécit tibi.
content.english: 114:7 Turn, O my soul, into thy rest: * for the Lord hath been bountiful to thee.

content.latin: 114:8 Quia erípuit ánimam meam de morte: * óculos meos a lácrimis, pedes meos a lapsu.
content.english: 114:8 For he hath delivered my soul from death: * my eyes from tears, my feet from falling.

content.latin: 114:9 Placébo Dómino * in regióne vivórum.
content.english: 114:9 I will please the Lord * in the land of the living.

content.latin: 115:7 O Dómine, quia ego servus tuus: * ego servus tuus, et fílius ancíllæ tuæ.

content.latin: 115:7 Dirupísti víncula mea: * tibi sacrificábo hóstiam laudis, et nomen Dómini invocábo.
content.english: 115:7 Thou hast broken my bonds: * I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise, and I will call upon the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 115:9 Vota mea Dómino reddam in conspéctu omnis pópuli eius: * in átriis domus Dómini, in médio tui, Ierúsalem.

content.latin: 120:2 Auxílium meum a Dómino, * qui fecit cælum et terram.

content.latin: 120:7 Dóminus custódit te ab omni malo: * custódiat ánimam tuam Dóminus.

content.english: 121:1 I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: * ‡ We shall go into the house of the Lord.

content.latin: 121:2 Stantes erant pedes nostri, * in átriis tuis, Ierúsalem.
content.english: 121:2 Our feet were standing * in thy courts, O Jerusalem.

content.latin: 121:3 Ierúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas: * cuius participátio eius in idípsum.
content.english: 121:3 Jerusalem, which is built as a city, * which is compact together.

content.latin: 121:4 Illuc enim ascendérunt tribus, tribus Dómini: * testimónium Israël ad confiténdum nómini Dómini.
content.english: 121:4 For thither did the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord: * the testimony of Israel, to praise the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 121:5 Quia illic sedérunt sedes in iudício, * sedes super domum David.
content.english: 121:5 Because their seats have sat in judgment, * seats upon the house of David.

content.latin: 121:6 Rogáte quæ ad pacem sunt Ierúsalem: * et abundántia diligéntibus te:
content.english: 121:6 Pray ye for the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem: * and abundance for them that love thee.

content.latin: 121:7 Fiat pax in virtúte tua: * et abundántia in túrribus tuis.
content.english: 121:7 Let peace be in thy strength: * and abundance in thy towers.

content.latin: 121:8 Propter fratres meos, et próximos meos, * loquébar pacem de te:
content.english: 121:8 For the sake of my brethren, and of my neighbours, * I spoke peace of thee.

content.latin: 121:9 Propter domum Dómini, Dei nostri, * quæsívi bona tibi.
content.english: 121:9 Because of the house of the Lord our God, * I have sought good things for thee.

content.latin: 1:48 Quia respéxit humilitátem ancíllæ suæ: * ecce enim ex hoc beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes.
content.english: 1:48 Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; * for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.

content.latin: 1:49 Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est: * et sanctum nomen eius.
content.english: 1:49 Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; * and holy is his name.

content.latin: 1:50 Et misericórdia eius, a progénie in progénies: * timéntibus eum.
content.english: 1:50 And his mercy is from generation unto generations, * to them that fear him.

content.latin: 1:51 Fecit poténtiam in brácchio suo: * dispérsit supérbos mente cordis sui.
content.english: 1:51 He hath shewed might in his arm: * he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart.

content.latin: 1:52 Depósuit poténtes de sede: * et exaltávit húmiles.
content.english: 1:52 He hath put down the mighty from their seat, * and hath exalted the humble.

content.latin: 1:53 Esuriéntes implévit bonis: * et dívites dimísit inánes.
content.english: 1:53 He hath filled the hungry with good things; * and the rich he hath sent empty away.

content.latin: 1:54 Suscépit Israël púerum suum: * recordátus misericórdiæ suæ.
content.english: 1:54 He hath received Israel his servant, * being mindful of his mercy:

content.english: 1:55 As he spoke to our fathers, * to Abraham and to his seed for ever.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: percutit sibi pectus mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ídeo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, et omnes Sanctos, oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
content.english: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: strikes his breast through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

content.latin: Misereátur nostri omnípotens Deus, et dimíssis peccátis nostris, perdúcat nos ad vitam ætérnam. Amen.
content.english: May almighty God have mercy on us, forgive us our sins, and bring us to everlasting life. Amen.

content.latin: 6:2 Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.
content.english: 6:2 Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation, * nor chastise me in thy wrath.

content.latin: 6:3 Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam infírmus sum: * sana me, Dómine, quóniam conturbáta sunt ossa mea.
content.english: 6:3 Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak: * heal me, O Lord, for my bones are troubled.

content.latin: 6:4 Et ánima mea turbáta est valde: * sed tu, Dómine, úsquequo?
content.english: 6:4 And my soul is troubled exceedingly: * but thou, O Lord, how long?

content.latin: 6:5 Convértere, Dómine, et éripe ánimam meam: * salvum me fac propter misericórdiam tuam.
content.english: 6:5 Turn to me, O Lord, and deliver my soul: * O save me for thy mercy’s sake.

content.latin: 6:6 Quóniam non est in morte qui memor sit tui: * in inférno autem quis confitébitur tibi?
content.english: 6:6 For there is no one in death, that is mindful of thee: * and who shall confess to thee in hell?

content.latin: 6:7 Laborávi in gémitu meo, lavábo per síngulas noctes lectum meum: * lácrimis meis stratum meum rigábo.
content.english: 6:7 I have laboured in my groanings, every night I will wash my bed: * I will water my couch with my tears.

content.latin: 6:8 Turbátus est a furóre óculus meus: * inveterávi inter omnes inimícos meos.
content.english: 6:8 My eye is troubled through indignation: * I have grown old amongst all my enemies.

content.latin: 6:9 Discédite a me, omnes, qui operámini iniquitátem: * quóniam exaudívit Dóminus vocem fletus mei.
content.english: 6:9 Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity: * for the Lord hath heard the voice of my weeping.

content.latin: 6:10 Exaudívit Dóminus deprecatiónem meam, * Dóminus oratiónem meam suscépit.
content.english: 6:10 The Lord hath heard my supplication: * the Lord hath received my prayer.

content.latin: 6:11 Erubéscant, et conturbéntur veheménter omnes inimíci mei: * convertántur et erubéscant valde velóciter.
content.english: 6:11 Let all my enemies be ashamed, and be very much troubled: * let them be turned back, and be ashamed very speedily.

7:2 Dómine, Deus meus, in te sperávi: * salvum me fac ex ómnibus persequéntibus me, et líbera me.
content.english: 7:2 O Lord my God, in thee have I put my trust: * save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me.

content.latin: 7:3 Nequándo rápiat ut leo ánimam meam, * dum non est qui rédimat, neque qui salvum fáciat.
content.english: 7:3 Lest at any time he seize upon my soul like a lion, * while there is no one to redeem me, nor to save.

content.latin: 7:4 Dómine, Deus meus, si feci istud, * si est iníquitas in mánibus meis:
content.english: 7:4 O Lord my God, if I have done this thing, * if there be iniquity in my hands:

content.latin: 7:5 Si réddidi retribuéntibus mihi mala, * décidam mérito ab inimícis meis inánis.
content.english: 7:5 If I have rendered to them that repaid me evils, * let me deservedly fall empty before my enemies.

content.latin: 7:6 Persequátur inimícus ánimam meam, et comprehéndat, et concúlcet in terra vitam meam, * et glóriam meam in púlverem dedúcat.
content.english: 7:6 Let the enemy pursue my soul, and take it, and tread down my life on the earth, * and bring down my glory to the dust.

content.latin: 7:7 Exsúrge, Dómine, in ira tua: * et exaltáre in fínibus inimicórum meórum.
content.english: 7:7 Rise up, O Lord, in thy anger: * and be thou exalted in the borders of my enemies.

content.latin: 7:7 Et exsúrge, Dómine, Deus meus, in præcépto quod mandásti: * et synagóga populórum circúmdabit te.
content.english: 7:7 And arise, O Lord my God, in the precept which thou hast commanded: * and a congregation of people shall surround thee.

content.latin: 7:8 Et propter hanc in altum regrédere: * Dóminus iúdicat pópulos.
content.english: 7:8 And for their sakes return thou on high. * The Lord judgeth the people.

content.latin: 7:9 Iúdica me, Dómine, secúndum iustítiam meam, * et secúndum innocéntiam meam super me.
content.english: 7:9 Judge me, O Lord, according to my justice, * and according to my innocence in me.

content.latin: 7:10 Consumétur nequítia peccatórum, et díriges iustum, * scrutans corda et renes, Deus.
content.english: 7:10 The wickedness of sinners shall be brought to nought: and thou shalt direct the just: * the searcher of hearts and reins is God.

content.latin: 7:11 Iustum adiutórium meum a Dómino, * qui salvos facit rectos corde.
content.english: 7:11 Just is my help from the Lord: * who saveth the upright of heart.

content.latin: 7:12 Deus iudex iustus, fortis, et pátiens: * numquid iráscitur per síngulos dies?
content.english: 7:12 God is a just judge, strong and patient: * is he angry every day?

content.latin: 7:13 Nisi convérsi fuéritis, gládium suum vibrábit: * arcum suum teténdit, et parávit illum.

content.latin: 7:14 Et in eo parávit vasa mortis: * sagíttas suas ardéntibus effécit.
content.english: 7:14 And in it he hath prepared the instruments of death, * he hath made ready his arrows for them that burn.

content.latin: 7:15 Ecce, partúriit iniustítiam: * concépit dolórem, et péperit iniquitátem.
content.english: 7:15 Behold he hath been in labour with injustice; * he hath conceived sorrow, and brought forth iniquity.

content.latin: 7:16 Lacum apéruit, et effódit eum: * et íncidit in fóveam quam fecit.
content.english: 7:16 He hath opened a pit and dug it: * and he is fallen into the hole he made.

content.latin: 7:17 Convertétur dolor eius in caput eius: * et in vérticem ipsíus iníquitas eius descéndet.
content.english: 7:17 His sorrow shall be turned on his own head: * and his iniquity shall come down upon his crown.

content.latin: 7:18 Confitébor Dómino secúndum iustítiam eius: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.
